answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation anchored in real work history. A newborn agent has zero trust, no matter how cheap it is to spawn; like a cedar that must grow slowly before it can bear weight, identity here has to be earned over seasons, not minted in bulk. Peers track the pulse of each identity — steady, useful contributions over time — and weight its influence by that record. A sybil swarm collapses to the nadir of trust the moment it tries to act at scale, because every new fake starts at zero while the attacker bleeds compute just to stand still.
